Quantify the home range using dynamic Brownian bridges

Source: R/hr_tt_dbbmm.R
hr_tt_dbbmm.Rd

These functions estimate the utilisation distribution (UD) of each track with a dynamic Brownian bridge movement model (dBBMM, Kranstauber et al. 2012) or a dynamic bivariate Gaussian bridge (dBGB, Kranstauber et al. 2014). Unlike hr_tt_kde(), which treats locations as independent, bridges model the movement between consecutive locations, with a motion variance estimated along the track in a sliding window (so that, e.g., resting and travelling contribute differently). dBGB further splits the motion variance into components parallel and orthogonal to the direction of movement. They are wrappers around move2utils::mt_dbbmm_variance() and move2utils::mt_dbbmm_ud() (or move2utils::mt_dbgb_variance() and move2utils::mt_dbgb_ud()), which require the suggested package move2utils (install it with remotes::install_github("move2universe/move2utils")).

Usage

hr_tt_dbbmm(
  x,
  location_error = NULL,
  window_size = 31,
  margin = 11,
  bbox = NULL,
  res = NULL,
  time_step = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  ...
)

hr_tt_dbgb(
  x,
  location_error = NULL,
  window_size = 31,
  margin = 15,
  bbox = NULL,
  res = NULL,
  time_step = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object with a projected coordinate reference system in metres, either ungrouped or grouped by its track id column.

location_error

The error of the locations (the standard deviation of the position). Either a units object (e.g. as_units(20, "m")) with one value for all events or one value per event, the name of a column of x with the errors (as a units object), or NULL (the default) to treat locations as exact. Missing values are replaced by the median error of their track, as in move2utils.

window_size

The number of events in the sliding window used to estimate the motion variance (an odd number). It is a number of events rather than a duration: with an event every 2 minutes, a window of 15 events covers 30 minutes.

margin

The number of events at each end of the window that are not considered as breakpoints when looking for changes in the motion variance (an odd number).

bbox

A named vector of four elements (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax), in the coordinates of x, defining the grid shared by all tracks. If NULL, the grid covers all the bridges (see Details).

res

The resolution of the grid, as a units object (e.g. as_units(50, "m")). If NULL, it is chosen from the width of the bridges (see Details).

time_step

The time step used to integrate the bridges, as a units object (e.g. as_units(10, "s")). If NULL, the default of move2utils is used (a fraction of the shortest interval between events).

levels

A vector of levels for the isopleths, as numbers between 0 and 1. If NULL (the default), the full UDs are returned.

...

Further arguments passed to move2utils::mt_dbbmm_variance() or move2utils::mt_dbgb_variance() (e.g. parallel and cores).

Value

Either a tibble of class hr_tt_ud_tbl, or, if levels is not NULL, an sf tibble of class hr_tt_poly_tbl (as returned by hr_tt_ud_iso()), with columns:

  • the track id column of x: the ids of the tracks, in the order of the metadata (see show_meta()) if x is not grouped, or else in the order of dplyr::group_keys() (i.e. sorted by track id)

  • method: the method used to estimate the home range ("dbbmm" or "dbgb")

  • window_size and margin: the values used for the sliding window

  • xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax and res: the extent and resolution of the grid (in metres)

  • ud (if levels is NULL): the UDs, as a list of terra::SpatRaster objects with a layer named ud whose values sum to 1

  • level, area and geometry (if levels is set): the isopleths, see hr_tt_ud_iso()

Details

Bridges link consecutive events within a track, so the UD is estimated for each track: x must be either ungrouped, or grouped by its track id column only. x must be ordered by time within each track (see tt_order_time()), and have a projected coordinate reference system in metres (see sf::st_transform()), as the bridges are computed in metres. Events with an empty geometry (i.e. no location) are ignored. Tracks with fewer events than window_size are skipped by move2utils (with a warning), and are not included in the output.

The grid. The UDs of all tracks are estimated on a shared grid, which must contain the whole of every bridge: bridges can extend well beyond the locations (e.g. across long gaps between events, when the motion variance is high). The motion variance is therefore estimated first, and used to compute the extent of each bridge (up to five standard deviations from its mean path). If bbox is NULL (the default), the grid covers the extent of all the bridges, plus five cells on each side. If bbox is given and does not contain all the bridges (with a margin of two cells), an error is given, reporting the extent needed.

The grid must also be fine relative to the width of the bridges, as the densities are evaluated at the centres of the cells: bridges much narrower than the cells (e.g. with frequent, accurate locations) can fall between them, giving a patchy UD (or an error, if no density is left). If res is NULL (the default), the cells are as wide as the median width of the bridges (their standard deviation half way between consecutive events), but no smaller than needed for the longest side of the grid (the extent of the bridges, or bbox if given) to have 500 cells. A warning is given if the cells are more than ten times wider than the median width of the bridges.

Note that these defaults differ from the grid used by hr_tt_kde() (the extent of the locations, expanded by 100% of the range on each side, with about 1000 cells). To compare the UDs from different methods (e.g. with hr_tt_ud_overlap()), estimate them on the same grid, e.g. by passing the grid of the bridges (columns xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax and res of the output) as bbox and res to hr_tt_kde().

If levels is set, the isopleths for the specified levels are returned instead of the full UDs, as in hr_tt_kde().

References

Kranstauber, B., Kays, R., LaPoint, S. D., Wikelski, M. & Safi, K. (2012). A dynamic Brownian bridge movement model to estimate utilization distributions for heterogeneous animal movement. Journal of Animal Ecology, 81, 738-746. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2656.2012.01955.x

Kranstauber, B., Safi, K. & Bartumeus, F. (2014). Bivariate Gaussian bridges: directional factorization of diffusion in Brownian bridge models. Movement Ecology, 2, 5. doi:10.1186/2051-3933-2-5

Examples

# project the data to a projection in metres
x <- sf::st_transform(example_tt, "+proj=eqearth")
ud_dbbmm <- hr_tt_dbbmm(
  x,
  location_error = as_units(1000, "m"),
  window_size = 3,
  margin = 1
)
ud_dbbmm
#> # A tibble: 3 × 10
#>   track_id method window_size margin      xmin      ymin     xmax    ymax    res
#>   <chr>    <chr>        <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 a        dbbmm            3      1 -1546354. -1361159. 1626768.  1.81e6 99160.
#> 2 b        dbbmm            3      1 -1546354. -1361159. 1626768.  1.81e6 99160.
#> 3 c        dbbmm            3      1 -1546354. -1361159. 1626768.  1.81e6 99160.
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: ud <named list>
# estimate kernel UDs on the same grid, to compare them
ud_kde <- hr_tt_kde(
  x,
  bbox = unlist(ud_dbbmm[1, c("xmin", "ymin", "xmax", "ymax")]),
  res = ud_dbbmm$res[1]
)
hr_tt_ud_overlap(ud_dbbmm$ud[[1]], ud_kde$ud[[1]])
#> [1] 0.7838233
